audience.programmeDescription: Econometrics and Data Science at the University of Amsterdam uses mathematics, statistics and programming to answer economic questions. This example follows the Econometrics specialisation and concludes with two linked thesis seminar courses.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR option combines economic modelling and econometrics. The other options emphasise algorithms and AI, or financial and organisational analysis. UvA has dedicated courses in actuarial mathematics, time series and microeconometrics.

componentNotes.y1-probability-statistics-1: UvA starts with a dedicated probability course. UCR studies probability alongside statistics.
componentNotes.y2-advanced-linear-algebra: UvA continues with advanced matrix methods. UCR’s Linear Systems course focuses on signals and systems.
componentNotes.y2-probability-statistics-3: UvA extends the statistics sequence to asymptotic theory and properties of estimators.
componentNotes.y1-intro-econometrics-actuarial: UvA introduces econometrics and actuarial science together.
componentNotes.y2-life-insurance: UvA requires specialised study of life insurance valuation.
componentNotes.y2-risk-theory: The example selects Risk Theory, which studies non-life insurance claims and the risk of an insurer running out of funds.
componentNotes.y2-econometrics-2: UvA develops a second econometrics course on issues including endogeneity, selection and censored data.
componentNotes.y3-time-series: UvA has a dedicated time-series course. UCR covers some work with temporal data and prediction in other courses.
componentNotes.y3-microeconometrics: UvA requires a separate course on advanced empirical methods for individual and firm behaviour.
componentNotes.y3-mathematical-economics-2: UvA continues with formal modelling of market structure and competition.
componentNotes.y3-open-space: This space allows 30 EC of approved electives, a minor, study abroad or a combination with an internship.
componentNotes.y3-thesis-skills: Students develop research and presentation skills alongside the thesis project.
componentNotes.y3-thesis: The research project leads to an individual thesis. UCR independent research is optional.

ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development
ACCPPDE101.text: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.

BENBUSI112.name: Accounting & Corporate Finance
BENBUSI112.text: Accounting & Corporate Finance introduces financial and management accounting, financial-statement preparation and analysis, costing, pricing, budgeting and organisational control. Students assess investment decisions using accounting measures, discounted cash flow, net present value, internal rate of return and cost of capital. A case study examines the misuse of an accounting principle and its effects on financial statements.

source.reviewNote: Read the selected current profile in full; the summary represents accounting, control and investment-appraisal content proportionately, without claiming an entire advanced corporate-finance sequence.

BENBUSI211.name: Business & Economy in the Age of AI
BENBUSI211.text: Examines AI's business, economic and societal implications without requiring a technical background. Students study AI's capabilities and limits, applications across business functions and industries, and effects on labour markets, productivity, innovation and inequality. Business cases and scholarly arguments support analysis of governance, regulation and a country's AI readiness and industrial policy.

BENBUSI312.name: Money, Banking & Finance
BENBUSI312.text: Examines financial markets, commercial banks and central banks, including interest rates, financial regulation, financial crises and monetary policy. Students analyse financial problems and manage a simulated bank in the Stanford Banking Game, using Excel dashboards and financial forecasts to inform decisions about loans, deposits, capital, liquidity and risk.

BENECON111.name: Introduction to Economics
BENECON111.text: Explore how individuals, firms, and societies make economic decisions. This course introduces key concepts from both microeconomics and macroeconomics, including markets, incentives, and the principles of supply and demand, and provides a foundation for analyzing real-world economic issues.

BENECON211.name: International Macroeconomics
BENECON211.text: Study the economy as a whole through topics such as national income, economic growth, inflation, and unemployment. Understand how governments and central banks use fiscal and monetary policies to influence economic performance over time. The course also explores business cycles, international trade, and economic crises, preparing students to evaluate policy debates and global economic trends.

BENECON212.name: Microeconomics & Behavior
BENECON212.text: Study how consumers and producers make decisions under scarcity. Explore key concepts such as rational choice, decision-making under uncertainty, and non-egoistic preferences. Analyze market structures, strategic interactions, and factor markets. Learn how markets function and examine the impact of regulation. Develop analytical tools to better understand behavior and engage with empirical research.

BENECON311.name: Public Economics
BENECON311.text: Investigate the role of government in the economy, focusing on how public policy influences efficiency and equity. The course covers taxation, public goods, externalities, and government spending. Combining theoretical models with empirical evidence, it evaluates how different policies affect societal welfare.

BENECON312.name: Econometrics
BENECON312.text: Econometrics supplies tools to analyze data to answer questions of causality and prediction. In this course you learn three estimators—Ordinary Least Squares, Generalized Least Squares, and Instrumental Variables—and three tests—t-test, F-test, and LM-test. Understanding the basic rules of econometrics, particularly the sampling distribution concept, is key, and the course uses Monte Carlo simulations in Stata to visualize it. Tools are applied to estimate economic relationships and make predictions, and students write an empirical paper.

source.reviewNote: CP071: read this complete displayed description and current course evidence. Retain accurate concise subject/method scope; no inferred extra topics, assessment or disciplinary equivalence. Official description retained verbatim.

BENECON314.name: Behavioral Economics
BENECON314.text: This course integrates insights from psychology into economic theory to better understand how people make decisions. Learn how actual behavior deviates from the predictions of traditional economic models due to biases, heuristics, and framing. Through experiments, students will deepen their understanding of decision-making and its implications for economic theory and practice.

BENENTR211.name: Marketing & Consumer Engagement
BENENTR211.text: Marketing & Consumer Engagement examines consumer psychology, marketing strategy, responsible brand development and customer engagement. Students analyse a company strategy, design a brand and investigate a consumer phenomenon using academic literature and primary and secondary evidence. Digital marketing and customer-journey mapping connect analysis with practical recommendations.

BENENTR212.name: Strategy & Digital Transformation
BENENTR212.text: The course explores how companies develop strategies and drive responsible digital transformation amid rapid technology change impacting the economy and society. Students develop a strategic plan, from vision to execution, and identify digital value opportunities. Using industry cases, they gain foresight into digital technologies and their impact on strategy, business models and social responsibilities.

BENENTR311.name: Market Research
BENENTR311.text: See how companies figure out what customers love and what they don’t. You’ll plan and carry out real research, analyze what you find, and share your results. Our course shows you how to gather opinions and turn them into smart business ideas—perfect for future marketers, analysts, or entrepreneurs.

BENGATE101.name: Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations
BENGATE101.text: Through experiential learning, students turn their own bold ideas into new ventures. No prior business expertise is required as teams work on a startup project from ideation to final pitch while gaining business and entrepreneurial skills in areas such as design thinking, business model and customer validation. The class fosters creativity and collaboration to drive business and social innovation.

BENGATE102.text: Research Methods & Statistics introduces research design, operationalisation, measurement, sampling, surveys and experiments. Students study descriptive statistics, estimation, hypothesis testing and introductory regression using R and R Commander. A group project develops a research plan and instruments, collects and analyses data, and reports findings under research-ethics and privacy requirements.

BENLEAD311.text: Psychology of Organizations & Leadership examines the psychological, social and structural dynamics of organisations. Case discussions and research-based frameworks address motivation, leadership, group dynamics, organisational culture, power, conflict and change.

DISARIN111.name: AI Ethics
DISARIN111.text: AI Ethics examines artificial intelligence from philosophical and psychological perspectives. Topics include fairness, privacy, responsibility, human-value alignment, moral status and political or existential risks. Students apply ethical frameworks to questions about human behaviour and interaction, synthesise research in an analytical psychology project, and produce a research-based podcast.

DISARIN211.name: Decision-making in AI
DISARIN211.text: Decision-making in AI examines how intelligent agents make decisions under uncertainty. Students study probability, Bayesian networks, temporal models, expected utility, Markov decision processes, partial observability and bandit problems. Multi-agent decisions and probabilistic programming extend the analysis, supported by equations, numerical examples and scientific papers.

DISARIN212.text: Introduces formal logic, abstract reasoning and proof. Students work with propositions, quantified statements, sets, Boolean algebra, functions and relations, direct and indirect proofs, induction and recursion. A final component models processes and games without chance and investigates winning strategies.

Topics include uninformed and heuristic search, local and global optimisation, adversarial search, constraint satisfaction, linear programming and discrete optimisation. Laboratory exercises and projects develop algorithm implementation, evaluation and experimental investigation of small intelligent systems.
